questions: Does the Integrator's controller for this iteration keep the oval and s-bend progress at or above the iteration 10 values (0.197 and 0.177)? If progress falls on either track, report which controller term caused it.
Does slalom steering_oscillation fall below 0.16 without a loss of slalom progress (iteration 10: 0.1626 and 0.1141)? If it does not, report whether the Integrator's kd change is the cause.
Do the metrics match iteration 10 to four decimals on all three tracks? If they do, geometry and controller are both at their verified values, and that should be recorded as the final result.
Per track, at what step and progress does the first line loss occur in the best run? Is it still at the start of the course or at a specific bend?

intent: Freeze the verified best platform (iteration 10 geometry, score 67.1299) for the final iteration. Keep the ±0.04 m, 16 mm row at y = 0.07 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_radius 0.03 m, and body 0.12 × 0.18 m. Expect any change in outcome to come from the controller, which the Integrator is tuning on this platform. Do not change geometry for the final unseen-track race, because the verified platform is the safest choice.
learning: Iterations 0 to 10 show that geometry has been exhausted for line loss on the oval and s-bend: spread, footprint, wheel track, wheel radius, lead and mass each left max_error at 0.060 to 0.069 m and line loss at one per trial. The controller is the first lever that has moved those tracks (kp 3.0, then kd near 0.2, lifting the score from 36.6 to 67.1). For the final unseen-track race, the platform should stay fixed at this verified geometry, and the controller should be the only change. The unresolved hypothesis is the mass midpoint of 0.65 kg, which would lower slalom oscillation. It was not tested because the expected score gain is small and the risk is unknown.
rationale:
Iteration 10 kept the iteration 9 geometry (±0.04 m row of 16 mm sensors at y = 0.07 m, wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.8 kg, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 × 0.18 m) and changed only the controller. Its score rose from 36.6227 to 67.1299. The oval progress rose from 0.115 to 0.197 and the s-bend progress from 0.040 to 0.177, though every trial still ended off track after one line-loss event. Slalom steering_oscillation was 0.1626, still just above the 0.16 threshold, and its progress was 0.114. Across spread, footprint, wheel track, wheel radius, lead and mass, the geometry tests left max_error at 0.060 to 0.069 m and line loss at one per trial. The controller change is the first lever to move the oval and s-bend, so geometry is no longer the binding limit on those tracks.

I considered the iteration 10 rule (b), which points to a mass midpoint of 0.65 kg if slalom oscillation stays above 0.16. I am not adopting it. Score does not reward low oscillation directly. Mass 0.5 kg in iteration 7 cut slalom progress and lowered the score by 0.67, and 0.65 kg is untested with the new gains. This is the final iteration, and the unseen track is scored once, so I am keeping the verified platform. Any change would carry risk for no measured score gain. The geometry is therefore unchanged from iteration 10, so the Integrator's controller work on this platform is the only variable under test.
